meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names satyajñānānandarūpā (Truth, knowledge and bliss), sāmarasyaparāyaṇā (Immersed in a state of steady wisdom), kapardinī (Wife of kapardi (Śiva, one with matted hair)), kalāmālā (Wearing all sixty-four forms of art as a garland), kāmadhuk (fulfills all desires), and kāmarūpiṇī (a desirable form). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು satyajñānānandarūpā, sāmarasyaparāyaṇā, kapardinī, kalāmālā, kāmadhuk, kāmarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names chandaḥsārā (Essence of all the vedas), śāstrasārā (Essence of all scriptures), mantrasārā (Essence of all mantras), talodarī (Slender-waisted), udārakīrtiḥ (possesses exalted fame), uddāmavaibhavā (She whose prowess is unlimited), and varṇarūpiṇī (the form of the letters of the alphabets). meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names kāryakāraṇanirmuktā (Free from the bond of cause and effect), kāmakelitaraṅgitā (Overflowing with pleasure in the union with kAmeshvara), kanatkanakatāṭaṅkā (Wearing glittering gold ear ornaments), līlāvigrahadhāriṇī (assumes various glorious forms as a sport), and ajā (no birth). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.

On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā (Skilled in raising those who are immersed in the mire of transmigratory life), yajñapriyā (Fond all sacrifices and other rituals), yajñakartrī (Doer of sacrificial rites), and yajamānasvarūpiṇī (the form of yajamAna, who directs sacrificial rites). meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā, yajñapriyā, yajñakartrī, yajamānasvarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā, yajñapriyā, yajñakartrī, and yajamānasvarūpiṇī do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse links divine grace with moral and cosmic order, showing that right action, consequence and sacred discipline belong within Her governance; Her fierce aspect is protective rather than arbitrary: what is destroyed is obstruction, ignorance or disorder that prevents dharma and freedom; the verse removes limitations one by one, reminding us that although She appears in form, Her absolute nature cannot be confined by any category. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names vīragoṣṭhīpriyā (Fond of the assembly of warriors), vīrā (Heroic), naiṣkarmyā (abstains from actions), nādarūpiṇī (the form of the primal sound), vijñānakalanā (realizes the knowledge of brahman), kalyā (Capable of creation), vidagdhā (Expert in everything), and baindavāsanā (Seated in the baindava (spot between the eyebrows) chakra). meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names caitanyārghyasamārādhyā (Worshipped with consciousness as the oblation), caitanyakusumapriyā (Fond of the flower that is consciousness), sadoditā (Ever shining), sadātuṣṭā (Ever pleased), and taruṇādityapāṭalā (Rosy like the morning sun). ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names viśvamātā (Mother of the universe), jagaddhātrī (Mother who protects and sustains the world), viśālākṣī (large eyes), virāgiṇī (Dispassionate), pragalbhā (Skillful and confident), paramodārā (Supremely generous), parāmodā (Supremely joyful), and manomayī (the form of the mind). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು viśvamātā, jagaddhātrī, viśālākṣī, virāgiṇī, pragalbhā, paramodārā, parāmodā, manomayī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. viśvamātā, jagaddhātrī, viśālākṣī, and virāgiṇī and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between the verse reveals another facet of the Mother’s nature and adds it to the cumulative vision of Lalitā as beauty, power, consciousness and liberation; the Mother is shown as origin, sustainer and intimate refuge, combining tenderness with the authority that guides beings toward freedom; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names daśamudrāsamārādhyā (Worshipped by ten mudras (sarva sa~NkShobhini, sarvavidrAvinI, sarvAkarshini, sarvavashankari, sarvonmAdinI, sarvamahankusha, sarvakhechari,…), tripurāśrīvaśaṅkarī (She for whom tripurAshrI is under control), jñānamudrā (the form of the j~nAna mudrA), jñānagamyā (To be attained through the yoga of knowledge), and jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇī (Both knowledge and the known). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು daśamudrāsamārādhyā, tripurāśrīvaśaṅkarī, jñānamudrā, jñānagamyā, jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. daśamudrāsamārādhyā, tripurāśrīvaśaṅkarī, jñānamudrā, and jñānagamyā and the remaining nāmas do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between Śiva and Śakti are presented as inseparable; consciousness and its power of manifestation are two ways of speaking about one Reality; Lalitā is not merely knowledgeable but is identified with consciousness and knowing itself, the light in which every act of understanding takes place; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.

ಭಕ್ತನಿಗೆ ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಮಟ್ಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ಯಾನಿಸಬಹುದು. ಆಪ್ತಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಲಿತೆ ಈ ವಿಶಿಷ್ಟ ಗುಣಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಆರಾಧಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ತಾಯಿ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯೆಯ ಆಳವಾದ ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೇ ಗುಣಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಗಳು—ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ, ಅಧಿಪತ್ಯ, ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕರುಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾತ್ಪರತೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳಲ್ಲ, ಒಂದೇ ಚೈತನ್ಯದ ಮುಖಗಳು.

meaning.en: This śloka presents Lalitā through the names ābālagopaviditā (Known well by all, even by children and cowherds), sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā (She whose commands are not disobeyed by anyone), śrīcakrarājanilayā (abides in shrIchakra, the king of chakras), and śrīmattripurasundarī (Divine tripurasundarI devI). The movement of the verse is cumulative: each nāma adds a distinct quality, so the Mother is seen at once through several complementary dimensions rather than through a single isolated attribute.
meaning.kn: ಈ ಶ್ಲೋಕವು ಲಲಿತೆಯನ್ನು ābālagopaviditā, sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā, śrīcakrarājanilayā, śrīmattripurasundarī ಎಂಬ ನಾಮಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ತುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ನಾಮವೂ ತನ್ನದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಅರ್ಥವನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದು, ಅವು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ಓದಲ್ಪಟ್ಟಾಗ ತಾಯಿಯ ಈ ಭಾಗದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ದೈವಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

deeper.en:
The deeper movement of this śloka becomes clearer when the names are read together. ābālagopaviditā, sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā, śrīcakrarājanilayā, and śrīmattripurasundarī do not simply form a list; they trace a relationship between royal language expresses spiritual sovereignty: every legitimate power and cosmic function ultimately rests within Her conscious rule; the verse expands Lalitā beyond a localized deity-form and identifies Her with the whole field of existence; the beauty of Her form is used as a devotional doorway that gathers the mind into loving concentration before leading it beyond all finite images. In that relationship, each name explains something the others leave unstated, so the verse becomes a compact theological portrait rather than a sequence of disconnected epithets.

For a devotee, the verse can therefore be contemplated on two levels at once. On the personal level, Lalitā is the Mother who can be approached, praised and loved through these particular qualities. On the deeper Śrīvidyā level, those same qualities point toward one indivisible Śakti whose beauty, authority, knowledge, compassion and transcendence are not separate powers but facets of a single consciousness.
